Fiona Grant: Heads-up  new preview: onprem-data-access-governance (DAG) for Private/VPC installs. Small, focused feature set to give customers fine-grained control over who/what can request exported data and how those exports are attested. :clipboard:
Fiona Grant: Why: customers with regulated export controls and data residency asked for session-scoped exports, consent records, and export attestations to hand to auditors.
Marco Ruiz: TL;DR features in preview:
- service-account scoping: map RBAC roles to export scopes
- session tokens: time-bound export tokens (STS-like)
- consent ledger: record customer consent or SLA-ack for each export
- signed export manifests: SHA256+signature bundle for any exported artifact
Helena Park: Activation: toggle dag.enabled in private-control-plane.yaml and supply a signing key. BYOK/HSM supported for air-gapped installs.
Fiona Grant: CLI example to request an export with consent (demo):
```
# request a sanitized audit bundle export, create a short session token
redwoodctl private dag request-export --tenant t-900 --scope audit:read --consent "SOC2-2026" --ttl 1h > export-request.json
# fetch manifest once ready
redwoodctl private dag fetch-manifest --id $(jq -r .request_id export-request.json)
```
Security: consent ledger entries are immutable and include the requestor identity, IP (if available), and a consent hash. If customer supplies the signing key, attestations are signed with the customer key.
Product Ops: Contract note: customers that want Redwood to manage long-term attestation storage must sign the "DAG Export Services Addendum". If they self-host attestations inside VPC, no addendum required.
Marco Ruiz: Emergency path: temporary export escalation requires explicit customer approval via the Console + two Redwood approvers. All escalations are recorded with reason and captured in the audit manifest.
Helena Park: Implementation detail: session tokens are short-lived JWTs issued by the private control plane and scoped to a single export target. The control plane validates tokens at export time and attaches X-DAG-Manifest header to successful exports.
Fiona Grant: UI: preview Console will show a DAG panel with active tokens, recent exports, and manifest hashes. Customers asked for a checkbox "require consent for support exports"  preview defaults to ON.
Security: For air-gapped setups we support an offline consent flow: customer-admin signs a consent blob and uploads it to the control plane; the control plane validates signature locally before issuing a session token.
Product Ops: Rollout plan: canary pk-staging-5 tomorrow 09:00 PT, limited preview invites in 10 days, GA after legal/compliance sign-off (target ~5-7 weeks).

Marco Ruiz: SRE note: ensure exporters surface X-DAG-Manifest in logs and that downstream storage handlers never persist raw PII when dag.scope excludes it. I'll add automated checks in the export pipeline.
Helena Park: Docs + runbook: drafting an internal ops runbook and a customer FAQ. Expect first draft by EOD Wed.
Fiona Grant: If you want to join preview testing or need a demo, ping @Product Ops or reply here. Label issues private-dag-preview.
